title: Can lookup compensate for a narrower FFN?
question: Can lexical lookup compensate for a narrower dense FFN at a declared endpoint?
hypothesis: Lookup may preserve some recall or completion behavior as dense FFN width narrows.
failure_interpretation: Recall or completion may survive while composition or override behavior deteriorates.
controls: Fix tokenizer, dataset source and packing within each selected data route.
Fix seed-matched model width, depth, heads, optimizer, runtime, budget, evaluator, and endpoint policy unless a listed axis changes.
Report held-out language-model loss separately from each capability card category.
confounders: Model-construction RNG changes when module inventories differ.
Approximate scale classes rather than matched parameter counts.
Educational-kernel overhead is not an architecture-speed measurement.
hardware_notes: Default guided lab; Tiny is recommended for a larger bounded trial, not a training-efficiency claim.
runtime_class: Qualitative scale-dependent educational PyTorch workload; measure local runtime rather than inferring timing.

papers.title: Engram
papers.claim_boundary: Motivates memory questions; SparseLab lexical memory is a local educational implementation, not a reproduction.

can_establish: All six declared raw outcomes and controlled endpoint deltas for width and memory contrasts.
cannot_establish: A one-variable narrow-plus-memory versus wide-plus-none ablation, training-efficiency claim, semantic/hybrid result, or cross-tokenizer equivalence.
prerequisites: Semantic and hybrid arms require later executable-memory prerequisites and are not generated.
